### Observed differences

- The clearest difference concerns A30, A31 and A36. In the earlier window each of the three occurred exactly once in every case (participation 100 in 100, mean about 1.0 occurrence per case, repeats in about 1 in 100 cases). In the later window they still occur in every case, but average about 3.5 occurrences per case, with repetition in about 68–69 in 100 cases. [OCC028, OCC029, OCC034]
- The routing at A36 changed accordingly: in the earlier window about 98 in 100 of A36's outgoing passes went to A25 and almost none returned to A30; in the later window about 71 in 100 return to A30 while about 28 in 100 still go to A25 — roughly one exit per case, as before. The internal edges A30→A31 and A31→A36 kept their shares (about 98–99 in 100) while their volume roughly tripled (about 200 to about 700 outgoing transitions each). [DIR036, DIR030, DIR031, OCC025]
- Ordering relations shifted from strict sequence to repetition: A14, still a once-per-case activity, co-occurs with A30 and with A36 in 100 in 100 cases in both windows, but a strict "A14 first" relation fell from about 99 in 100 cases to about 32 in 100, replaced by interleaved/repeated patterns (about 68 in 100); A30 versus A36 shows the same shift (strict order from about 98.5 to 31.5 in 100). For A05, present in about half the cases, strict precedence to A30/A36 fell from about 54 in 100 cases to about 17, with interleaving rising to about 34 in 100. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL002, REL003]
- Short-range repetition pairs appeared: A36 followed by A30 within five steps is now seen in about 136 of 200 cases (1 before), and A30 followed by itself in about 136 (1 before), while the tight two-step A30→A36 gap, previously present in about 96 in 100 cases, covers only about 12 in 100 later cases. [LAG004, LAG002, LAG003]
- The event positions of the repeated activities spread out: the positional standard deviation of A30 rose from about 0.06 to about 0.12 and of A36 likewise, and A14's spread also grew (about 0.02 to 0.05) with a slightly earlier mean position. [POS003, POS004, POS002]
- Away from this block, A05 occurs slightly less often (55 to 51.5 in 100 cases) and earlier; its outgoing passes shifted from A14 (35 to 18 in 100) towards A07 (19 to 39 in 100), and the A05→A14 gap widened. [OCC005, POS001, DIR005, LAG001]
- Smaller shifts: A06 now appears in more cases (13 vs 23 of 200), A21 participation fell (52.5 to 46 in 100) while A22 rose (47.5 to 54 in 100), and A15/A16 repeat slightly more often (about 44 vs 37 in 100 cases). Several rarely observed activities (A02, A04, A08, A10, A45) show large reshuffles of outgoing transitions on only about 4–25 observed passes, which is weakly grounded. [OCC006, OCC021, OCC022, OCC015, OCC016, DIR002, DIR004, DIR008, DIR010, DIR045]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the sequence A30 → A31 → A36, which previously ran exactly once per case and then exited to A25, is now executed as a repeating loop: in the later window A36 returns to A30 in about 71 in 100 of its passes, so the trio runs about 3.5 times per case on average — about 69 in 100 cases repeat it while the rest still run it once — before a final A36→A25 exit that still occurs about once per case. A14 keeps its single occurrence and still accompanies the block in every case; its ordering classification changed only because the block now repeats. [DIR036, DIR030, DIR031, OCC028, OCC029, OCC034, OCC014, REL004]

The signs agree and are direct: all three activities had 100 in 100 participation in both windows, so this is not a rare variant surfacing in one sample; the back edge A36→A30 is observed directly in the successor profiles; the relation, lag and position items show the same repetition pattern (strict order giving way to interleaving, new short-range A36→A30 and A30→A30 pairs, doubled positional spread). These items describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [DIR036, REL004, REL006, LAG002, LAG004, POS003, POS004]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show what ends the loop or whether the number of iterations is bounded, and it cannot distinguish a newly added A36→A30 edge from an existing edge that was rarely taken before (about 1 in 200 earlier passes). No screening expectation is present in the evidence, so the judgement rests on the directness and consistency of the repetition signal rather than a chance comparison. [DIR036, OCC028]

Other differences: A05 occurs less often and earlier and routes to A07 instead of A14; A06 appears in more cases; A21 and A22 move in opposite directions; A15/A16 repeat slightly more often; several low-frequency activities show weakly grounded outgoing-profile reshuffles. [OCC005, DIR005, POS001, LAG001, OCC006, OCC021, OCC022, OCC015, OCC016, DIR002, DIR045]
